before.description_long:
ChatGPT is OpenAI's flagship chat assistant for writing, coding, research, analysis and multimodal tasks. It works in the browser, in desktop and mobile apps, and through the API.

As of October 2026, ChatGPT runs GPT-6 with a new Intelligent UI, which rolled out on October 7, 2026 to Plus, Pro, Business and Enterprise, and October 8 to Free and Go. Paid plans use GPT-6 Sol in the main chat, while Free and Go use GPT-6 Luna. GPT-6 Astra is OpenAI's most capable model. GPT-6.1 Sol, released September 29, 2026 at OpenAI's DevDay, is available only in ChatGPT Work and Codex for Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise and Edu plans, not in the main chat interface. GPT-5.5 was retired from ChatGPT, Work and Codex on October 14, 2026.

Capabilities span long-form and technical writing, code generation and debugging, document and image analysis, voice conversations, web browsing, data analysis and image generation. The Intelligent UI lets answers include graphics, tappable buttons, forms, charts, maps and small interactive tools such as calculators and games built on the spot. An always-on agent feature called Dots, with its own cloud computer and browser, is available on Pro for users over 18 outside the EEA, UK and Switzerland, as well as on Business Premium and Enterprise.

Pricing is tiered. Free costs $0/mo and runs GPT-6 Luna. Go costs $8/mo and Plus costs $20/mo. Pro is offered in three monthly tiers at $100, $200 and $500 per month, with the $500 tier adding Ultrafast mode for Codex and Work. Business costs $25 per user per month, or $20 per user per month billed annually. Enterprise and Edu pricing is available on request, and API usage is billed per 1 million tokens, varying by model.

Limitations remain: the newest model, GPT-6.1 Sol, is not yet available in the main chat interface, only through Work and Codex. GPT-5.5's retirement removes an option some users relied on. The assistant can still produce confident but incorrect answers, and Dots is restricted by age, region and plan.

ChatGPT suits anyone who wants a general-purpose AI assistant, from individual users on the free plan to professionals and teams who need higher usage quotas, advanced reasoning or business and enterprise features.

before.description: OpenAI Codex is OpenAI's coding agent that writes, fixes, refactors and reviews code from the ChatGPT apps, the open-source Codex CLI, an IDE extension and Codex cloud. It is included in ChatGPT plans, with full access starting at Plus for $20 a month.
before.description_long:
OpenAI Codex is a software engineering agent rather than an autocomplete tool. You hand it a task, such as tracking down a bug, refactoring a module, adding a feature or writing tests, and it works through the codebase, runs commands and returns changes for you to review. The same agent is available in the ChatGPT desktop, web and mobile apps, in the terminal through the Codex CLI, in an IDE extension and in Codex cloud, all connected through your ChatGPT account.

As of October 2026, OpenAI's Codex pricing page lists GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Sol, GPT-6 Luna and GPT-6 Astra as the models used in Codex. GPT-5.5 was retired from Codex for ChatGPT sign-in on October 14, 2026. In June 2026 OpenAI said Codex had more than 5 million weekly active users, and JetBrains research published in August 2026 put Codex's work adoption at 16% in May to July 2026, up from 3% in January.

Codex can run several agents in parallel, use computer and browser tools to check its own work, and keep working on cloud tasks after you close your laptop, with reusable cloud environments for each repository. It can automatically review pull requests, surface findings and answer questions about them. It connects to GitHub, GitLab (beta), Slack and Linear and can be extended with plugins. The Codex CLI is open source under the Apache-2.0 license and installs on macOS, Linux and Windows, and a Codex SDK and the codex exec command support scripting.

Codex is included in ChatGPT plans. Free ($0) and Go ($8 a month) include lightweight Codex use in the desktop app with GPT-6 Luna, subject to rollout. Plus ($20 a month) adds Codex on the web, in the CLI, the IDE extension and on iOS, with GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Luna. Pro costs $100, $200 or $500 a month and currently has no five-hour usage limit. Business is $20 per user per month billed annually for 2 or more users, or $25 per user billed monthly, and Enterprise and Edu are priced through sales. Plus, Pro and Business users can buy extra credits, and Codex can also run with an API key at standard API rates.

The main limitation is usage. On Plus and Business, Codex is capped per five-hour window, and heavier models use the allowance much faster: OpenAI estimates roughly 15 to 160 local messages per five hours with GPT-6.1 Sol, against 350 to 3,000 with GPT-6 Luna. Free and Go only get the lightweight Luna model in the desktop app. Codex works only with OpenAI models, and as with any coding agent, its changes and its shell and repository access need careful review and permission settings.

Codex suits developers and teams who already pay for ChatGPT and want one agent across the terminal, the editor and the cloud, and teams that want AI review on every pull request. Developers who prefer Anthropic's models or want to switch between vendors should also look at Claude Code, Cursor or GitHub Copilot.

before.description: GitHub Copilot is an agentic, multi-model coding assistant that goes beyond autocomplete, offering chat, an agent mode, cloud agents, code review and a CLI, with models available from vendors including Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, xAI, Microsoft and Moonshot. It bills usage through GitHub AI Credits, with tiers running from a free plan up to individual and organization plans.
before.description_long:
GitHub Copilot started as an in-editor autocomplete tool, but the current product is a full multi-model coding platform. It lives inside your editor, in the terminal, in a desktop app, and on GitHub itself, handling code completion, chat, an agent mode that edits across files, cloud agents that work on tasks asynchronously, and automated code review.

GitHub has repositioned Copilot around a new desktop app pitched as taking issues all the way to merge, and billing now runs on consumption-based GitHub AI Credits rather than flat request units. Paid plans include both a base monthly credit allowance and an optional flex allowance that adds extra included usage at no additional charge, and higher tiers can now delegate work to third-party coding agents such as Claude by Anthropic and OpenAI Codex, currently in preview.

The core capabilities are agent mode, cloud agents, chat, code review, a CLI, and the ability to pick from models across multiple vendors including Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, xAI, Microsoft and Moonshot. Inline code completions and Next Edit suggestions stay included on every plan and do not draw down your AI Credits allowance.

On pricing, individuals can choose Free at $0 per month (about 2,000 inline suggestions, limited chat and agent usage, no code review or cloud agents), Pro at $10 per month (includes $15 worth of usage through a base plus flex allotment, roughly 1,500 AI Credits, with unlimited inline suggestions, code review and cloud agents), Pro+ at $39 per month (includes $70 worth of usage, roughly 7,000 AI Credits, and adds delegation to third-party coding agents), or Max at $100 per month (includes $200 worth of usage, roughly 20,000 AI Credits, with priority access to premium models). One AI Credit equals $0.01, and additional credits can be purchased on paid plans if you exceed your included allotment. Verified teachers and maintainers of popular open source projects can get Pro for free.

The main limitation is cost predictability once you exceed your included AI Credits: extra credits are billed separately, so heavy agent, chat or premium-model use can cost more than the listed subscription price. GitHub also notes that flex allotments may change over time, so the amount of included usage isn't fixed. Admin budgets and spending caps can help organizations control this, but teams still need to monitor consumption closely.

Copilot is a strong fit if you already work in GitHub and VS Code, want an agentic assistant rather than plain autocomplete, and value being able to choose from models across different vendors. The free tier is a low-risk way to try it, while Pro+ and Max suit heavier users who want premium models and third-party agent delegation.

before.description_long:
Gemini is Google's family of AI models and the consumer assistant built on top of them, available on the web, in the mobile app, and inside Workspace apps like Gmail, Docs and Sheets. It handles conversation, document analysis, image generation, coding and live voice interaction.

As of October 2026 the flagship model is Gemini 4 Argon, announced September 30, 2026 for vetted cyber defenders and made generally available on October 13, 2026. The newest Flash model is Gemini 3.8 Flash, which reached general availability on September 2, 2026, and the current image model is Nano Banana 2.1, released October 6, 2026. Canva AI is the AI layer inside Canva, the browser-based design platform used for social posts, presentations, documents, and marketing assets. It runs on the Canva Design Model and introduced Magic Layers, which splits an AI-generated poster back into separate, editable layers; Magic Layers is also available inside ChatGPT and Gemini.

The most recent addition is Canva Craft, Canva's first in-house image-generation model, built by Canva Research and launched October 22, 2026, available to all Canva users globally through Dream Lab. Craft uses a two-stage architecture, in which a planning model writes a composition plan and a rendering model draws it, producing images at up to 2K resolution across 30 or more aspect ratios with text rendering in 55 languages, built to work well with Magic Layers. Craft is also reachable through Canva's Public API, with access via Canva's MCP server listed as coming soon. Canva says Craft debuted 4th on the DesignArena image-generation leaderboard, which it describes as making Canva Research the 2nd-ranked lab for image generation.

Magic Studio bundles the rest of the toolkit: Magic Design for templates, Dream Lab (now powered by Craft) for image generation, Magic Write for copy, Canva Sheets and Magic Charts for data-to-visualization plus Magic Insights, and Magic Switch, which does AI-driven layout redesign rather than simple resizing. The assistant keeps persistent memory and stays aware of your brand assets.

It suits solo creators, small marketing teams, social media managers, and non-designers who want good-looking, on-brand assets fast without learning a professional design tool.

before.description_long:

Agents are available to everyone on n8n Cloud running the latest stable version and to self-hosted Community users with extra setup, while Enterprise support for them is still in preview; they sit alongside the existing AI Agent node rather than replacing it.

AI and agent workflows remain a major focus: the AI Agent node supports structured tool calling against models from providers including Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Mistral and Groq. Recent releases have also added dozens of new native integrations, bringing the total past 500, along with per-node retry with exponential backoff, a new Browser Use capability, expanded admin controls, public API access and additional enterprise authentication options.

Pricing is tiered. The self-hosted Community Edition is free, with unlimited executions and access to all integrations; n8n's cloud service offers a free trial (1,000 executions, no credit card required) but has no free ongoing plan. Cloud AI credits are capped and can run out on heavy agent workloads, and the highest self-hosted tier (Business) is not currently offered as a cloud plan. Workflows can also get complex enough to require a real learning curve beyond simple no-code tools.

before.description_long:
Claude Code is Anthropic's agentic coding tool. It reads your codebase, edits files, runs commands and can carry a task from a plain-language request through to a working change, rather than just suggesting completions in an editor.

The current release is CLI 2.1.302, published October 16, 2026. The default model is Claude Opus 5.5 across Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise and the Anthropic API. Anthropic's own documentation describes Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Fable 5 as the most capable models available in Claude Code, though they are not the default and must be selected explicitly.

Beyond the terminal, Claude Code also runs as VS Code and JetBrains extensions, as a desktop app and on the web. It supports cloud agents, subagent orchestration, computer use, scheduled cloud agents (Routines), background subagents and an Auto mode available on Pro and on Bedrock, Google Cloud and Microsoft Foundry. Code Review, a GitHub pull-request review feature for Team and Enterprise plans, left research preview and became generally available on October 15, 2026, with Quick, Standard and Deep review levels that admins choose per repository.

Pricing: the Free tier ($0) does not include Claude Code. It is bundled into Pro ($17/month billed annually or $20/month billed monthly), Max (from $100/month, billed monthly only, with a higher-usage tier also available), Team Standard ($20/seat/month billed annually or $25/seat/month billed monthly, for teams of 2 to 150) and Team Premium ($100/seat/month billed annually or $125/seat/month billed monthly). Enterprise is priced at $20/seat/month billed annually (20-seat minimum) plus usage at API rates. Separate pay-as-you-go API pricing per million input/output tokens includes Claude Fable 5.1 at $10/$50 (selected explicitly, not default), Claude Opus 5.5 at $4/$20 (default; a faster mode runs at roughly 2x standard pricing, $8/$40), Claude Sonnet 5.5 at $2/$10, and Claude Haiku 5.5 at $0.10/$0.50 for prompts up to 100K tokens ($0.50/$2.50 above), now the default Haiku model on the Anthropic API.

Limitations are worth knowing. There is no free way to use Claude Code, usage caps apply even on paid plans, and heavy agentic runs on the API can get expensive. High-effort agent runs can also be slow and consume tokens quickly.

It suits professional developers and teams who want an agent that actually edits and ships code, especially those already on a Claude Pro, Max or Team plan who want coding included without a separate API bill.

before.description_long:

Grok and Cursor now share a single weekly usage pool for subscribers on this plan. Key capabilities include the Composer agent for large edits, cloud agents and cloud dev environments triggered with /in-cloud, automatic code review, and Bugbot for automated PR review. It still supports third-party models, MCP servers, custom rules, and hooks, so you are not locked into any single model family. Recent additions include Projects (beta), self-hosted machines, and Rollouts and Security Review bots for Teams and Enterprise customers.

Under The X Subscription, Cursor is offered in five tiers: Free, Plus at $8 per month, Premium at $30 per month, Super at $100 per month, and Ultra at $200 per month. These tiers draw on a shared weekly usage pool for Grok and Cursor. As of October 2026, Photoroom offers a Free plan and four paid plans: Pro, Max, Ultra and Enterprise. Paid plans combine unlimited core tools (within fair use) with a monthly pool of AI credits for heavier generation features. On its website the company says it is trusted by 80M+ users and 1M+ businesses.

Core tools include the Background Remover, Retouch, AI Product Fixer, preset AI Shadows, AI Fill, AI Expand and Resize, Image Enhancer and Recolor. Credit-based tools include AI Backgrounds Studio, AI Fashion Models, AI Images, Edit with AI, adjustable AI shadows and the Video Generator. Pro and Max yearly plans include a 7-day free trial, each paid plan includes an API and MCP credit wallet worth the plan's price, and prices and credit amounts vary by country.

The Free plan has limited features, lower credit and export limits, no API access and is for personal, non-commercial use only. before.description_long:
Freepik started in Málaga in 2010 as a search engine for free graphic resources and grew into one of the largest stock libraries for photos, vectors, icons and templates. On April 28, 2026 it rebranded as Magnific, the name of the AI upscaling startup it acquired in May 2024, to bring its stock library, generative AI tools and upscalers under one brand. freepik.com now redirects to magnific.com.

Magnific says it has more than 1 million subscribers. Rather than relying only on its own models, it gives subscribers access to leading third-party models, including Kling, Seedance, Google Veo, Gemini Omni, MiniMax, Nano Banana, FLUX, Recraft, Ideogram and Grok for images and video, plus Google Lyria and ElevenLabs for music and sound effects. In October 2026 it added Magnific One, its own image model, together with a Brand Kit feature.

Beyond generation, Magnific includes Spaces, a shared canvas for building workflows, pro editing tools for image, video and design, the Magnific image and video upscalers, music, voice and sound effect generation, custom AI characters on paid plans, an MCP server and plugins, a ComfyUI integration, API access and metadata export. The stock library of more than 250 million photos, videos, vectors and PSDs is part of the same subscription.

The Free plan has no credits but allows daily use of basic AI tools: up to 20 image generations, 40 sketch-to-image conversions, 3 retouch, expand or reimagine actions, 1 background removal and 1 icon generation a day, plus 10 stock downloads a day, for personal use with attribution. Premium includes 20,000 credits a month (240,000 a year on annual billing), all premium stock, 100 downloads a day and a commercial license, with no option to buy extra credits. Premium+ includes 45,000 credits a month (600,000 a year), unlimited generation on most image models, music rights and the option to buy extra credits. Pro comes in two tiers with 112,500 or 300,000 credits a month (1.5 million or 4 million a year) and adds a merchandise license and early access. Business covers teams of up to 100 seats at 45,000 credits per seat a month, and Enterprise is custom. Prices are shown in local currency and vary by region, annual billing is much cheaper than monthly, and promotions are frequent.

There is no single published price list in US dollars, so check the pricing page for your region before subscribing. Credit costs vary widely: a Nano Banana image at 2K resolution uses 75 credits, while 4 seconds of Seedance video at 1080p uses 4,400 credits. Unlimited generation covers most image models, but video, audio and editing tools still use credits. Free use is personal only and requires attribution, and the rebrand means older Freepik links and guides now point to Magnific.

Magnific suits designers, marketers and agencies who want stock content and many AI models in one subscription, especially for high volumes of images. If you only need one image model, Midjourney, Leonardo AI or Krea AI may be simpler, and Adobe Firefly fits teams already using Adobe Creative Cloud.
